page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top ("VARIA POEMATA.") with page number 103 at top right. Below it, one poem titled AD UXOREM., set as six stanzas of verse, followed by the author's initials I. I. B. at right. A gathering signature "G. iij." at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: AD UXOREM.
main_text.p: TE proles solito cur numerosior Imis sollicitam pectoribus tenet Uxor, coniugii quam mihi propriam Fecit perpetuo fœdere castitas.
Horres exigui pauperiem laris Quem non pascit ager, non domus, aut pecus Latum: nec posita magna pecunia Occulto reditu fœnora nutriunt
Gens mentis Superūm nescia prouidæ, Gens quæ forte regi cuncta putat vaga, Demens, ancipiti concutitur metu Cum rerum dubios prospicit exitus.
Sed summum æthereis sedibus Optimi Regnare arbitrium credidimus Patris. Hic certum genitis auxilium feret: Hic larga tribuet quod satis est manu.
Nil prouisa iuuat copia diuites, Si deest superi gratia Numinis. Si præsens placido lumine recreat Detestata nihil pauperies nocet.
Hinc pectus trepidis intrepidum geris Rebus, qui sceleris purus & integer Vitæ, rite tuum supplice dextera Numen, summe Pater, quod colit, inuocat.

page.notes: The initial T of TE is a large woodcut-style letter joined to the first word. Long s has been transcribed as s throughout. The line "Superūm" carries a tilde over the u for a left-out m. The printed hyphen-less line ends and punctuation are otherwise as printed. The signature "G. iij." is the gathering mark at the foot.
